subject: machine-paced-delivery
seam: scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:285 (`if (payload.stop_hook_active) process.exit(0)`) + the three-state exit contract at :248-266, wired via .claude/settings.json hooks.Stop
seam_note: This gate corrected the technique twice. It mutates nothing and BLOCKS nothing (its own header: 'Nothing here ever blocks') -- and it still guards re-entry, because exit 2 feeds a reminder to the model, the model acts, acting ends another turn, and the turn end re-fires the hook. So the termination contract is created by the gate's output RE-ENTERING THE AGENT'S LOOP, not by blocking and not by mutation; advisory is the weakest tier and the one most likely to ship unguarded. Technique redrafted twice mid-run to the three-tier form (advisory / blocking / mutating). Second corroboration: the hook's recorded history is the liveness paragraph made concrete -- it detected nothing for its entire life, replayed over all 31 transcripts, 1,136 Edit/Write calls, ZERO detections, because its turn-boundary scan stopped at the first user-role entry and 3,837 of 4,187 user-role entries are tool results. Ran green every turn and was indistinguishable from a working gate. Reached gate-liveness's three-state contract (0 pass / 2 model-actionable / 3 could-not-run) independently, after being burned by exactly that failure.
ship_reason: the gate already implements the technique's re-entry rule; nothing to change -- this is a confirming tree, read-only
return_condition: counters on the re-entry path and the could-not-run path, both currently unobservable: a gate that has never reported a skip and a gate whose skip path is broken look identical
